clue.text: English portico included in refurbishing of yard always

indicators.note: included in says the English portico is placed inside the reworked letters
refurbishing means doing up, so the letters of 'of yard' are rearranged

parts.note: a veranda is a roofed porch or portico along a house

explanation.surface: A yard is being done up, and an English-style porch is going into it for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'portico' sends the mind to columns, but it is just a roofed porch; the reworked yard wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning eternally or for an endlessly long time.

clue.text: Furniture maker's application in two languages

definitions.meaning: a glossy shellac finish that cabinetmakers rub onto wood
the tongues of France and of Poland, placed side by side

explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is a link: the answer is a cabinetmaker's finish, and also read as two words it is a pair of European languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a shellac finish applied to furniture; the second names two national languages.

clue.text: University man supports the artist in one element

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
a don is a university lecturer or fellow

explanation.surface: A college lecturer props up a painter inside some single element.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, DON 'supports' RA by sitting beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive noble gas is one of the chemical elements of the periodic table.

clue.text: Diver's rig treated with bluish coating

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain letters with the S included

explanation.surface: A scuba diver's kit has been treated against a bluish film.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'Diver's' counts: DIVERS plus RIG gives the nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the greenish-blue patina that forms on copper and brass as they weather.

clue.text: Wireless mainly took in to give out

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so the old radio term loses its last letter

parts.note: wireless is the old British word for a radio set
to take food in is to eat it, so the past tense gives ate

explanation.surface: Someone mostly listens to the wireless and absorbs things before passing them on.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to emit or send out, as heat or light is given out.

clue.text: Gossip about one who's dressed more smartly

indicators.note: about means going round, so the chat word is wrapped around the numeral

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip idly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: People are chatting about somebody who turns out better dressed than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and dapper, so the comparative describes someone dressed more stylishly.

clue.text: Where horses are is like a small shelter

parts.note: as can mean like, in the sense of in the manner of
a cot or cote is a small shelter for animals or birds

explanation.surface: The place horses are kept resembles a little hut.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is an English racecourse in Berkshire, famous for its royal race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous racecourse, so it is a place where racehorses are found.

clue.text: In cooperation with a spun out cricket team?

parts.note: something spun out is drawn out, made long
a side is a team, as in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a drawn-out cricket match makes a fitting partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Working alongside someone means working together with them, in cooperation.

clue.text: A shrub of greater age

definitions.meaning: a small tree or bush with white flowers and dark berries
older, the comparative used of family members

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a berry-bearing bush and also means older, as an older sibling.

clue.text: Device to sense when to turn off includes time in firm

indicators.note: includes says the word for putting off holds the next part inside it

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off doing something

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for time within the firm

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A gadget senses the moment to switch off, with a timer built into the company's design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; 'to turn off' reads like switching a device off, but it means discouraging someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A detector is an instrument built to sense or discover something, such as smoke or metal.

clue.text: Set off, content but ready to react violently

parts.note: to trigger something is to set it off
content means satisfied, happy

explanation.surface: Something has been set off, and everyone seems pleased but jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone too quick to shoot or lash out aggressively.

clue.text: Frank's one in the play

parts.note: frank means open and honest, candid
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A man called Frank has a role in the stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a man's name but means candid. CANDIDA is a comedy by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a George Bernard Shaw comedy about a clergyman's wife.

clue.text: A number could be entering namelessly

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else
N is the abbreviation for name, so namelessly drops one N

explanation.surface: A number might be keyed in without anyone's name attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'namelessly' removes one N from ENTERING, leaving ETERING, which 'could be' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part.

clue.text: In response, fires operative back a difficult question

indicators.note: back says the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, run on across them

explanation.surface: A working rifle answers fire, posing a tricky problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'fiRES OPerative' lies RESOP; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling or awkward question that is hard to answer.

clue.text: Hate rocks when crushed and prefer to eat this?

definitions.text: Hate rocks when crushed and prefer to eat this?

indicators.note: crushed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hates rock cakes crushed and would rather eat something else.
explanation.walkthrough: HATE and ROCKS together are rearranged; the whole clue suggests a crumbly biscuit one might choose instead of rock cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a crumbly sweet biscuit, the sort of treat one would prefer to eat.

clue.text: One being in science fiction

parts.note: the word sci-fi aliens use for an inhabitant of our planet

explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction aliens call a human from our planet by this name.

clue.text: Gleanings of its use?

parts.note: gleanings are what is gathered from the fields, the product of a farm machine at work

explanation.definitionFit: A combine or reaping machine gathers crops, and gleanings are what is gathered in.

clue.text: Appearance with instrument? Get a move on!

parts.note: a look is an appearance
a sharp is a pointed instrument such as a needle or scalpel

explanation.surface: Someone's look is paired with a musical instrument, and they are told to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' tempts towards music, but a sharp here is a cutting or piercing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an urgent command to hurry up and be quick.

clue.text: Lose oar at sea? Could be the spray

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rower drops an oar overboard and gets a faceful of spray.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a fine spray of liquid, or the can that releases it.

clue.text: Entrances allies, including soldiers with troop leader

indicators.note: including says the word for friends holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: pals are friends or allies
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Friends and soldiers, together with a troop commander, file through the gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Portals are grand doorways or gateways, ways in.

clue.text: Old official with first lady following on

indicators.note: following says the woman's name comes after the other piece

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: An old official arrives with the President's wife coming along behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or steward in medieval England.

clue.text: Left dog around one living in new country

indicators.note: around says the gundog's name goes round the abbreviation for left

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A dog left behind wanders round a pioneer's new home.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a colonist who makes a home in a newly opened land.

clue.text: Retainer's part of the flat charge

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the fixed fee goes to the household servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retainer' suggests a servant or a fee, but it is a fastening that retains a door; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a catch that retains or holds a door or gate shut.

clue.text: Quiet after Rhine trips? It's the wine!

indicators.note: after says the hushing word comes behind the rearranged letters
trips suggests stumbling about, so the river's letters are rearranged

parts.note: sh is the sound used to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: After a trip down the Rhine, all is quiet and the wine flows.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhenish is an old name for Rhine wine, hock, so the river supplies the wine's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish is an old term for wine from the Rhine region.

clue.text: Copy of journal that's sent round

indicators.note: sent round says the abbreviation is placed around the magazine word

parts.note: IE stands for id est, that is
mag is short for magazine, a journal

explanation.surface: A copy of a magazine is being circulated.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or copy of something.

clue.text: Fellow worker going to the Continent for music

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A colleague heads off to Europe to make music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Continent' usually means mainland Europe to the British, but here it is Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasia is a free-form musical composition.

clue.text: Parking vehicle before a long walk

indicators.note: before says the vehicle comes ahead of the parking letter

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: After parking the car, someone sets off on a hike.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring walk or hike.

clue.text: A small cut is required in this theatrical performance

definitions.text: A small cut is required in this theatrical performance

parts.words: A small cut is required in this theatrical performance
parts.note: the theatre is the operating theatre, where a minimally invasive procedure goes in through a tiny incision

explanation.walkthrough: 'theatrical performance' suggests drama, but the theatre is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: This minimally invasive surgery is done through very small incisions.
